newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares end up in technical rebound.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares end up in technical rebound.

text.p: Brazilian stocks ended slightly higher Friday in a technical correction, helped by an improvement in U.S. stocks, brokers said.
"Yesterday's drop was exaggerated, that's why the market bounced back. But Wall Street's gains also helped," one trader said.
The Bovespa index .BVSP of the 49 most-active shares closed up 0.61 percent at 69,978 points. Market turnover rose to a moderate 310.9 million reais (US$299.1 million).

Analysts noted, however, the CPMF tax issue prevented the market from moving much higher today. The federal government is expected to announce next week whether stock market transactions will be subject to the CPMF tax which will take effect Jan 25.
The tax will levy a 0.2 percent charge on financial transactions to raise about $400 million a month for Brazil's health service.
Among the big winners, state mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce and state oil firm Petrobras outperformed the Bovespa index, rising 2.56 percent and 2.13 percent, respectively.

The power sector index .IEE, made up of the nine most traded stocks of the electrical sector, rose 1.31 percent, ending at 1,960 points, with Minas Gerais state power utility Cemig leading the rise by gaining of 2.47 percent.
The new Brazil index or IBX, comprising the 100 most traded shares, rose 0.45 percent to 1,535 points.
